content:
Apple's annual sales in India are reported to have surpassed US$10 billion for the first time in the most recent fiscal year.

This achievement is particularly remarkable in a country where the average annual income is less than US$3,000 — especially considering that iPhones are priced higher in India than in the United States…

For years, iPhone sales in India were negligible for Apple. But the situation has shifted dramatically in recent years, as local economic development has finally allowed Apple to open dedicated stores in the country.

Bloomberg reported this latest milestone today.

Given India's low per capita income and the fact that iPhones are actually manufactured in India, one might expect local prices to be far lower than those in the United States. In reality, however, hefty taxes make Apple products more expensive in India than in the US.

Apple offsets some of this burden by partnering with banks to offer credit card rebates.

Currently, about a quarter of iPhones are manufactured in India, but most of those are shipped to the US market. Apple restructured its logistics arrangements specifically to circumvent US tariffs imposed on Chinese imports.
